szoveg_eredeti:
President Donald Trump’s push for “super intelligence” threatens the American way of life.

Trump signed an executive order last month to replace the term “artificial intelligence” with “super intelligence” in all federal communications. According to a White House press release, “super intelligence” better represents a promised future of American technological progress.

While AI signifies the ability of a machine to perform tasks that historically required human intelligence, SI signifies a future in which machines’ abilities surpass that of human beings.

Renaming AI to SI does not yet represent a true qualitative difference. But the name shift implies a possible future that falsely assumes increasingly powerful inventions will lead to more human liberty.

If we really want to be free, we should call artificial intelligence what it is: artificial.

We should never allow a tool of our own making to control us if we want to preserve our freedom. If we rely on SI to create poetry and music, we will become slaves to a machine while weakening our innate capabilities.

Politicians often frame the AI battle as the lesser of two evils — a technological arms race against China that America must win to preserve its greatness. But running the AI arms race risks contorting America into a homogenized country that has increasingly adopted the state-run surveillance and sterility of our political enemy. There is something ironic about fighting China by relying on the same transnational tech elites that created these technologies.

Two men who refer to themselves as “early AI adopters” warned about how AI will transform human life in a 2025 essay for The Free Press.

The essay, co-authored by economist Tyler Cowen and tech policy expert Avital Balwit, claims we are at the threshold of the “most profound identity crisis humanity has ever faced,” because machine intelligence will soon surpass human intellectual abilities.

Cowen and Balwit predict a future in which a select group will have unimaginable control. But they suggest that for most people, life will become “less spontaneous, and also less proactive. These individuals may quite literally feel like ‘cogs in the machine.’”

People are drawn to controlling the world. It may seem now that calling AI “SI” marks the extent of human progress and how much we can control. But that’s not what we should pursue.

Ernst Jünger, a World War I veteran who lived to the age of 102, understood the fundamental difference between human and technical perfection.

His 1957 novel, “The Glass Bees,” imagines a world where the brilliant businessman Zapparoni invented marionette-like automatons of technical perfection. Yet Jünger argues that striving for technical perfection sacrifices human perfection, which he saw as incalculable.

“Perfect mechanisms — around which, therefore, stands an uncanny but fascinating halo of brilliance — evoke both fear and Titanic pride which will be humbled not by insight but only by catastrophe,” he writes. “The fear and enthusiasm we experience at the sight of perfect mechanisms are in exact contrast to the happiness we feel at the sight of a perfect work of art…that arms and legs are lost or harmed is not yet the greatest danger.”

Men who prioritize machines champion anti-human “progress,” and referring to a robot as “super intelligence” does exactly that. Our nation’s official terminology should reflect the artifice that is technology, which is different from our embodied flesh and blood.

Wendell Berry, the late Kentucky farmer and writer, said the world’s next great division will be “between people who wish to live as creatures and people who wish to live as machines.”

We should strive to be the first set: people who live as creatures. The first step is recognizing our place in the world, which must avoid the self-imposed slavery of “super intelligence.”

Sophia Mandt is a senior studying sociology and social thought.

prioritas.lead_hu: Egy amerikai egyetemi lap véleménycikke szerint Donald Trump elnöki rendelete a szuperintelligencia kifejezés használatáról veszélyezteti az amerikai életformát.
